$comment: Detector sidecar for the canonical rule registry (PLAN.md, Fase 1). One entry per canonical rule id. type: detector (a deterministic tool proves the PRESENCE of the violation) | ausencia (proves only the ABSENCE of a guard — weaker proof, reported separately) | juicio (a model decides with a closed question) | fuera (declared, never deleted). Post-audit 2026-10-06: query prose and confidence removed; spec is structured per tool and must parse (validated by scripts/validate-detectors.mjs). The census is PROVISIONAL until positive/negative fixtures pass per rule. Validate: node scripts/validate-detectors.mjs. SCOPE FIELDS (added 2026-10-08, defect 6a): a field that looks like a scope but does nothing is a lie in the schema. A `gitleaks` spec's `path_regex` is consulted ONLY by isHistoryPathSpec (scripts/detect/matchers.mjs), which tests it against `.git/` to route the spec to the git-history scan; for a working-tree spec the runner (runGitleaksLite in scripts/detect/engine.mjs) walks every text file and IGNORES path_regex. A working-tree gitleaks spec must therefore NOT carry one. Optionally, a spec may carry a free-text `note` stating its real scope; `note` is not executed.

code-god-package-9.reason: Reclassified detector -> juicio on 2026-10-08 (defect 3). The rule's condition is PACKAGE-level ("god_package_detected (> 50 files in package)", skills/code-quality-assessment.skill.md), but the spec it carried was a max-occurrences count of `(?m:^package\s+\w+\s*$)` with max 50 — a count of matches INSIDE one file. A valid Go file contains exactly one `package` clause, so the only input that could fire was an INVALID Go file with 51 concatenated clauses (measured: realistic store.go -> 0 findings; 51 concatenated `package pN` lines -> 1 finding). No matcher in the node-matcher vocabulary counts files per package, and fixing it needs a new matcher in scripts/detect/matchers.mjs plus a new entry in the COMPLEXITY/MATCHERS registry — a new tool, not a spec correction. It is left for a model with repo access (Fase 3) rather than approximated, exactly like the structure-* coupling/cycle rules (structure-high-coupling-1 and 30 other repo-level structural rules are `juicio`). No fixture can exist for a `juicio` rule: the engine runs no tool for it, so a positive/negative pair would be evidence for nothing.

spec.note: WHOLE-TREE scan, stated plainly (defect 6a, 2026-10-08). This spec carried a path_regex of `(?i:workflows?|n8n)/.*\.json$` that the runner IGNORES: runGitleaksLite (scripts/detect/engine.mjs) walks every text file in the tree and only consults path_regex to route a spec to the git-HISTORY scan (isHistoryPathSpec, which tests the regex against `.git/`). Measured before removal: it fired on config/settings.json and on src/legacy.js, i.e. outside any workflows/ directory. The field was a scope that did nothing, so it is deleted rather than kept as a lie in the schema; the rule is global by declaration now, and the positive fixture carries a non-workflow file so that behaviour is asserted instead of assumed. Re-adding a real scope means implementing path filtering in runGitleaksLite first.
